reason: Connecting retinal sensing to the clock addresses the first part of the goal.
expectation: I expect a pathway carrying light information to the brain clock, though its effect on the nighttime signal may come later.

alternatives.reason: The nerve route and gland also seem necessary, but I prefer to start with the light input.

effect: The retinal cells provide light information that helps synchronize the brain clock; I can now connect its output route.
reaction: The distinction between sensing light and keeping the clock in step is useful.
reason: Connecting the clock to the nerve route seems a direct next step toward the nighttime signal.
expectation: I expect a clock-linked nerve pathway, possibly still needing the pineal gland.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the nerve route to the gland first also seems plausible, but I prefer to extend the clock pathway.

effect: The clock's outgoing route reaches the marked pineal location via an indirect pathway, so the gland is the next connection.
reaction: The route through the spinal cord and neck is an unexpected detail, though its purpose is not yet explained.
reason: This is the only offered combination and connects the gland to the clock pathway.
expectation: I expect the pineal gland to join the pathway, possibly revealing how it sends a nighttime signal.

effect: The completed pathway shows that the pineal gland releases more melatonin at night and that light can suppress it; I can now connect it to the body.
reaction: The day-and-night comparison makes the signal clearer, although melatonin's effects are not explained.
reason: This is the only offered combination and connects the pathway to the existing body.
expectation: I expect the body model to gain the connected clock and pineal pathway, possibly completing the goal.

effect: The pathway is now connected to the body, and the chapter adds that the brain clock helps coordinate rhythms in other organs through several routes.
reaction: The wider connection is useful, though those other routes remain unexplained.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the pineal gland was most worthwhile: the planned day/night comparison connects the pathway to melatonin release and shows light suppressing it at night.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the finished pathway to the body was comparatively thin: it mentions several routes coordinating organs but does not explain them.

surprise.text: The outgoing nerve route travels indirectly through the spinal cord and a neck nerve cluster before reaching the pineal location.

arbitrary.text: No combination felt purposeless, but the reason for the indirect route was not explained. The compatible-option menu guided the choices rather than requiring discovery of compatibility.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in another chapter to see how melatonin and the clock affect body rhythms, although the largely sequential assembly offered few meaningful choices.
